clips.send: Velocity. Speed in a direction. Velocity is speed together with its direction, for example 10 m/s east. The green arrow above each car shows its velocity: a longer arrow means faster, and it points the way the car moves. When a car reverses, its velocity becomes negative: the arrow flips to point backwards.

clips.send: Speed. How fast: distance divided by time. Speed equals distance divided by time. The SI unit is meters per second (m/s). Average speed equals total distance divided by total time. Instantaneous speed is the speed at one moment, like a speedometer reading. 10 m/s is 36 km/h, about as fast as a quick bicycle.
clips.text: Speed. How fast: distance ÷ time. Speed = distance ÷ time. The SI unit is meters per second (m/s).. Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. Instantaneous speed is the speed at one moment, like a speedometer reading.. 10 m/s is 36 km/h, about as fast as a quick bicycle.

clips.send: Common mix-up: A car driving around a curve at a steady 20 m/s has a constant speed but a CHANGING velocity, because its direction keeps changing.
clips.text: Common mix-up: A car driving around a curve at a steady 20 m/s has a constant speed but a CHANGING velocity, because its direction keeps changing.

clips.send: Common mix-up: A flat line on a distance–time graph means the object is STOPPED. A flat line on a speed–time graph means it is moving at a STEADY speed. Always read the y-axis first!
clips.text: Common mix-up: A flat line on a distance–time graph means the object is STOPPED. A flat line on a speed–time graph means it is moving at a STEADY speed. Always read the y-axis first!

clips.send: Acceleration. How fast velocity changes. Acceleration equals change in velocity divided by time: a equals (v_end minus v_start) divided by t. Unit: m/s squared (meters per second, every second). a equals 2.5 m/s squared means the velocity grows by 2.5 m/s every second. Slowing down is also acceleration (pointing backwards, negative). Turning is acceleration too.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Speed has no direction. 10 m/s north and 10 m/s south are the same SPEED but different VELOCITIES.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Speed has no direction. 10 m/s north and 10 m/s south are the same SPEED but different VELOCITIES.

clips.send: Time. Measured with the stopwatch. Time is measured in seconds (s), the SI unit. On motion graphs, time always goes on the horizontal x-axis. To find a speed you need two measurements: a distance AND the time it took.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Run one 400 m lap and stop where you began: distance equals 400 m, displacement equals 0 m. Turn on “Allow reversing” to see this on the track.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Run one 400 m lap and stop where you began: distance = 400 m, displacement = 0 m. Turn on “Allow reversing” to see this on the track.

clips.send: Displacement. Change in position, with a direction. Displacement tells how far and in which direction you end up from your starting point. The cyan arrow on the track points from the start line to each car: that is the car’s displacement. If you come back to where you started, your displacement is 0 m, even though your distance is not.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Acceleration does not mean “going fast”. A car cruising at a steady 30 m/s has ZERO acceleration.

clips.send: Distance. How much ground is covered. Distance is the total length of the path an object travels. Its SI unit is the meter (m). Distance never goes down: even driving backwards adds to it, like a car’s odometer. The marker posts on this track are 10 m apart, and the whole strip is 100 m long.
